_comment: Pattern library for corpus generation. Each technique carries the concept it teaches, observable signals, and several DISTINCT scenarios (different context, not v1/v2 clones). Educational descriptions only - no payloads, no live targets, no flags.

_schema.concept: the one idea a learner should walk away with
_schema.signals: observable clues that point at this technique
_schema.first_checks: safe local things to look at before reaching for tools
_schema.scenarios: distinct framings of the same underlying pattern

techniques.concept: User input reaches a SQL query as code rather than as data.
signals: response changes on a quote character
first_checks: read the query construction in source
compare responses for a true vs false condition
scenarios: Login form concatenates the username directly into a WHERE clause.
Product filter builds an ORDER BY clause from a query parameter.
Legacy admin search endpoint interpolates a LIKE pattern without escaping.
REST API passes a JSON field into a raw query for a report export.
Password-reset lookup trusts an email parameter inside a subquery.

techniques.concept: An injectable SELECT can be extended to read from other tables once column count and types line up.
signals: injection point inside a SELECT that renders rows
first_checks: count the columns the page renders
identify which rendered column accepts text
scenarios: Search results page reflects rows directly from a single SELECT.
CSV export endpoint renders arbitrary columns it is handed.
Paginated listing exposes the underlying query through a sort parameter.
Public API returns rows as JSON, making column types easy to probe.

techniques.concept: Even with no output, a difference in behaviour is a single bit of data per request.
first_checks: find any observable difference between true and false
measure baseline response time
scenarios: Login returns the same generic message but different HTTP status.
Coupon-check endpoint returns valid/invalid with no error detail.
Availability API answers only yes or no for a given identifier.
Rate-limited endpoint leaks state through response timing alone.

techniques.concept: Input concatenated into a template is evaluated as template syntax, not printed as text.
signals: template engine name in stack traces
first_checks: test whether a trivial expression renders as its result
identify the engine from error output
scenarios: Greeting page builds the template string from a display name.
Email templating service renders a user-supplied subject line.
Error page interpolates the requested path into the template source.
Report generator lets users define their own header format.
Notification system renders admin-configured message templates.

techniques.concept: Joining user input onto a base path lets the input walk back out of it.
signals: filename or path in a parameter
first_checks: find where the path is joined
check whether normalisation happens before or after validation
scenarios: Download handler joins a filename parameter onto an uploads directory.
Static asset route serves files by a user-controlled relative path.
Language selector loads a translation file named by a cookie value.
Log viewer opens files under a directory chosen by a query string.
Archive extractor writes entries using paths taken from the archive.

techniques.concept: If the token says which algorithm to verify with, the token controls verification.
signals: alg field honoured from the header
verification library called without an allowlist
first_checks: decode the header and payload
find where the library is told which algorithm to accept
scenarios: API accepts a token whose header declares no signature algorithm.
Session middleware verifies with whatever algorithm the header names.
Microservice trusts an internal token without re-checking the algorithm.
Mobile backend falls back to unverified decode when verification errors.

techniques.concept: A public key is public; using it as a symmetric secret collapses the trust model.
signals: RS256 tokens plus a reachable public key
one verify call handling both key types
first_checks: locate the public key
check whether the verifier distinguishes asymmetric from symmetric
scenarios: Service publishes its RSA public key at a well-known JWKS endpoint.
Certificate embedded in the client bundle is also the verification key.
Token verifier passes the key through a single generic verify helper.
Key rotation endpoint exposes historical public keys.

techniques.concept: Authentication that can be satisfied by data the user controls is not authentication.
signals: trust in a header set by the client
first_checks: list everything the client sends that the server trusts
look for the authorization check, not just the login
scenarios: Admin panel checks a role claim the client can set.
Internal endpoints trust an X-Forwarded-For style header for origin.
Session id is derived from a timestamp and a username.
Debug parameter left in production skips the auth middleware.

techniques.concept: Knowing an identifier is not the same as being allowed to use it.
signals: object fetched before ownership is checked
first_checks: map which identifiers appear in requests
check whether ownership is verified after lookup
scenarios: Profile API fetches by a sequential numeric user id.
Invoice download accepts any document id from any account.
Support ticket thread is keyed only by an incrementing number.
File-sharing link uses a short predictable identifier.

techniques.concept: Output encoding is context-dependent; HTML-escaping does not protect a JavaScript context.
signals: escaping applied for the wrong context
first_checks: find where the input lands in the response
identify the context: HTML body, attribute, or script
scenarios: Search page echoes the query term back into the results heading.
Error message renders an unescaped parameter inside an attribute.
Analytics snippet inlines a campaign parameter into a script block.
Redirect notice prints the destination URL into the page body.

techniques.concept: A server fetching a URL for you is a request that carries the server's trust, not yours.
signals: server-side fetch of a user URL
allowlist done on the string not the resolved address
first_checks: identify what the server can reach that you cannot
check whether validation survives redirects
scenarios: Link preview feature fetches whatever URL a user submits.
Webhook tester performs an outbound request to a configured endpoint.
PDF renderer loads remote images referenced in user HTML.
Image proxy resizes pictures fetched from arbitrary addresses.

techniques.concept: XML parsers that resolve external entities turn a document into a file-read primitive.
first_checks: identify the parser and its entity settings
check whether a DOCTYPE is accepted at all
scenarios: Document import endpoint accepts XML from users.
SVG upload is parsed before it is rendered.
SAML assertion consumer parses attacker-influenced XML.
Legacy SOAP API left entity resolution enabled.

techniques.concept: Deserializing untrusted bytes can construct objects, and constructing objects runs code.
signals: serialized blobs in cookies or parameters
first_checks: identify the serialization format from its header bytes
find where the blob is deserialized
scenarios: Session cookie carries a serialized object rather than an id.
Cache layer stores serialized objects keyed by user input.
Message queue consumer deserializes payloads from an open topic.
Remember-me token is a signed but attacker-influenced object graph.

techniques.concept: A check and the action it guards are two events; anything can happen in between.
signals: balance or quota checked then modified
no transaction or lock around the pair
first_checks: find the check and the write
ask what a second request between them would see
scenarios: Gift-card redemption checks the balance before decrementing it.
One-per-user signup bonus verifies then inserts without a constraint.
File upload validates a name before writing it to disk.
Vote endpoint counts existing votes before recording a new one.

techniques.concept: Recursive merges over untrusted keys can reach shared object internals.
first_checks: find recursive merge functions
check whether special keys are filtered
scenarios: Settings endpoint deep-merges submitted JSON into defaults.
Query-string parser builds nested objects from bracket notation.
Plugin loader clones user configuration into a shared object.
Template context is merged from multiple untrusted sources.

techniques.concept: Writing past a fixed buffer overwrites the stack state that tells the CPU where to return.
signals: no bounds check on a length
first_checks: check protections with checksec
find the input path and the buffer size
scenarios: Menu-driven program reads a name into a small fixed buffer.
Parser copies a length-prefixed field without validating the length.
Legacy service reads a line into a stack array with no limit.
Config loader copies an environment variable into a local buffer.
Network handler reuses a stack buffer across differently sized messages.

techniques.concept: When you cannot run your own code, run code that is already there.
first_checks: confirm NX and PIE state
identify what leaks an address
scenarios: Overflow exists but the stack is non-executable and libc is dynamic.
A format-string bug leaks a libc pointer before the overflow.
Binary prints a function pointer during normal operation.
Partial overwrite is possible because only the low bytes vary.

techniques.concept: Short instruction sequences ending in a return can be strung together into a program.
signals: no convenient single function to call
first_checks: inventory available gadgets
work out the minimum chain that changes memory permissions
scenarios: Statically linked binary offers gadgets but no useful imported call.
Overflow is large enough for a chain but the binary is stripped.
Only a short write primitive exists, so the chain must be staged.
Sandbox restricts syscalls, narrowing which chain is viable.

techniques.concept: A format string taken from input is an interpreter for reading and writing memory.
signals: user data passed as the format argument
first_checks: find printf-family calls with a non-literal format
observe what leaks from a benign specifier
scenarios: Logging helper passes the user message straight to printf.
Error handler formats an attacker-influenced string for display.
Debug build prints a banner assembled from an environment variable.
Echo service formats input before writing it back.

techniques.concept: A canary only helps if the attacker cannot learn it or can avoid crossing it.
first_checks: confirm the canary is present
look for a leak that runs before the overflow
scenarios: A read primitive discloses stack contents before the write happens.
Child processes inherit the same canary across forks.
An index bug writes past the canary without touching it.
Byte-at-a-time output lets the value be recovered incrementally.

techniques.concept: Randomised layout stops guessing, not leaking; one real address often reveals the rest.
first_checks: identify any address the program reveals
check which bytes of an address stay constant
scenarios: Program prints a heap pointer in a diagnostic message.
Only the low twelve bits are fixed, enabling a partial overwrite.
An uninitialised read discloses a leftover stack address.
Repeated connections reuse the same layout in a forking server.

techniques.concept: Allocator metadata lives next to your data, so overflowing data corrupts bookkeeping.
signals: size and copy length come from different places
first_checks: map the allocation lifecycle
compare the requested size against the copied size
scenarios: Note manager copies content using a length from the previous record.
Struct with an inline buffer is resized without reallocating.
Off-by-one null byte overwrites the neighbouring size field.
Custom pool allocator keeps free-list pointers inside user data.

techniques.concept: Freeing memory without clearing the pointer leaves a handle to someone else's data.
signals: delete option that does not null the pointer
first_checks: track which pointers survive a free
look for an allocation that can land in the freed slot
scenarios: Menu program deletes an entry but keeps the reference.
Object with a virtual table is freed while still registered in a list.
Cached connection struct is reused after close.
Double free corrupts the free list before reallocation.

techniques.concept: Arithmetic on sizes wraps, so a validated length can still produce a tiny allocation.
signals: size computed by multiplication or addition
first_checks: find the arithmetic before the allocation
test the boundary values of the type
scenarios: Array allocation multiplies count by element size without a check.
Signed length is compared against a maximum then used as unsigned.
Offset plus length wraps, passing a range check it should fail.
Sixteen-bit counter truncates a larger user-supplied count.

techniques.concept: A single byte past the end is enough when that byte is structurally important.
first_checks: read the loop bounds carefully
check who writes the string terminator
scenarios: Copy loop runs one iteration too many on the buffer length.
Null terminator is written just past the allocated size.
Index validation permits the length value itself.
Fixed-size record parser assumes a trailing separator exists.

techniques.concept: A one-byte key has 256 possibilities, so scoring plausible plaintext beats cleverness.
first_checks: score every candidate key against English frequency
look for the most common byte
scenarios: A short ciphertext file with no header and no structure.
Hex-encoded blob embedded in a script's constant.
Obfuscated configuration value in a binary's data section.
Encoded string stored inside a QR payload.

techniques.concept: Key reuse turns one hard problem into many easy single-byte problems.
signals: repeating structure at a fixed stride
ciphertext much longer than any plausible key
first_checks: estimate key length from repeated distances
split into columns and solve each independently
scenarios: Long text encrypted with a short word as the key.
Log file obfuscated with a fixed repeating key.
Firmware strings masked with a cycling key byte pattern.
Two messages encrypted under the same key stream.

techniques.concept: Without padding, a small exponent on a small message never wraps the modulus.
first_checks: check the size of e
compare the ciphertext magnitude against the modulus
scenarios: Exponent three is used with a short unpadded message.
The same message is sent to several recipients with small e.
Textbook RSA is used to encrypt a numeric code.
Signature verification omits padding checks entirely.

techniques.concept: Two coprime exponents over one modulus let you combine ciphertexts without the key.
first_checks: compare moduli across the provided keys
check whether the exponents are coprime
scenarios: One message is encrypted twice under different exponents.
A key server reuses the modulus across two user accounts.
Migration kept the old exponent alongside a new one.
Backup key shares the modulus of the production key.

techniques.concept: RSA's security rests entirely on factoring being hard for that particular modulus.
signals: modulus appears in a public database
first_checks: check the bit length
test whether the primes are near the square root
scenarios: The modulus is small enough to factor directly.
The two primes were generated adjacently and sit close together.
Two keys share a prime factor, revealing both.
A weak random source produced a repeated prime.

techniques.concept: Any observable difference between 'bad padding' and 'bad content' leaks the plaintext.
first_checks: confirm the mode of operation
check whether the two failure modes are distinguishable
scenarios: Decryption API returns different messages for padding and MAC errors.
Timing differs measurably between the two failure paths.
Cookie decryption raises a distinguishable exception.
Error pages differ only in status code between the two cases.

techniques.concept: ECB encrypts identical blocks identically, so alignment turns encryption into a lookup table.
first_checks: look for repeated 16-byte blocks
check whether you control data before the secret
scenarios: Profile cookie encrypts attacker data followed by a secret.
Encrypted upload preserves duplicate blocks from a known image.
Token format places user input immediately before a fixed suffix.
Bulk encryption of records reveals duplicate rows.

techniques.concept: Merkle-Damgard hashes can be continued from a digest, so secret-prefix MACs are forgeable.
first_checks: determine how the MAC is constructed
identify the hash family
scenarios: API signs requests with a hash of a secret prepended to parameters.
Download link integrity uses a secret-prefix digest.
Session data is authenticated by concatenation rather than HMAC.
Legacy signing scheme predates the move to HMAC.

techniques.concept: Substitution preserves letter frequency and word shape, which is exactly what breaks it.
first_checks: run a frequency count
look for single-letter and common short words
scenarios: A paragraph of English with letters consistently swapped.
A puzzle keeps spacing, making word patterns visible.
A keyword-derived alphabet with repeated structure.
Numbers left in the clear alongside substituted letters.

techniques.concept: With only 25 shifts, exhaustive search is the correct first move.
first_checks: print all 25 shifts
check for a flag prefix in each
scenarios: A short message shifted by a fixed amount.
ROT13 applied twice to different halves of the text.
A shift applied only to letters, leaving digits untouched.
Nested shift inside a base64 layer.

techniques.concept: Identify the encoding from its alphabet and padding before trying to decode anything.
first_checks: inspect the alphabet in use
check the length modulus
scenarios: A string using only base64's alphabet with trailing padding.
Uppercase base32 text that looks like nonsense words.
Percent-encoded text nested inside a JSON field.
A decimal or binary representation of ASCII bytes.
Base58 text with no lookalike characters.

techniques.concept: Decoding is iterative; each layer tells you what the next one is.
signals: decoded output that is itself valid encoded text
gzip magic bytes after a decode
first_checks: decode one layer and re-examine
check magic bytes at every stage
scenarios: Base64 wrapping hex wrapping a compressed blob.
Repeated ROT and base64 alternation over many rounds.
URL encoding hiding a base32 payload.
A QR code whose payload is itself an encoded document.

techniques.concept: Strings that are absent from the binary are usually built at runtime by a small routine.
signals: a loop over a data blob near startup
first_checks: run strings and note what is missing
find cross-references to the data section
scenarios: Password is compared after an XOR decode of a data blob.
Error messages are assembled character by character at runtime.
A lookup table maps indices to decoded text.
Strings are decoded lazily on first use and cached.

techniques.concept: The goal is understanding the transformation well enough to invert it, not reading every instruction.
signals: a check function comparing against a constant
first_checks: find the comparison and work backwards
search constants against known algorithm tables
scenarios: A licence check applies a reversible transform before comparing.
A serial validator sums and rotates digits in a fixed pattern.
Input is hashed with a custom function and matched to a constant.
A checksum routine mirrors a well-known algorithm with tweaked constants.

techniques.concept: Anti-debugging checks are ordinary code paths and can be understood like any other branch.
first_checks: compare behaviour with and without a debugger
locate the check before the divergence
scenarios: The program exits early when a tracer is attached.
A timing check detects single-stepping and alters results.
Breakpoint bytes are detected via a self-checksum.
The binary behaves differently when a debugger environment variable is present.

techniques.concept: A packer replaces the real code with a stub that reconstructs it, so find the moment after unpacking.
first_checks: check entropy per section
look for a known packer signature
scenarios: A standard packer with a well-known unpacking utility.
A custom stub that decompresses into freshly allocated memory.
Only part of the binary is packed, leaving a readable loader.
The entry point jumps into a section marked writable and executable.

techniques.concept: A bytecode interpreter moves the logic into data, so recover the instruction set first.
signals: a byte array driving control flow
first_checks: identify the dispatch loop
map opcodes to handlers one at a time
scenarios: A custom interpreter validates the input through bytecode.
Handlers are dispatched through a table of function pointers.
The bytecode is itself decrypted before execution.
A stack machine implements the comparison logic.

techniques.concept: Flattening hides order, not logic; recovering the state transitions restores the original flow.
signals: a single loop with a large switch
a state variable assigned in every block
first_checks: find the state variable
record which state each block sets next
scenarios: All basic blocks are reachable only through one dispatcher.
State values are computed rather than assigned as constants.
Opaque predicates add branches that never actually execute.
Only the validation routine is flattened, not the rest of the program.

techniques.concept: A capture is a transcript; follow the conversation rather than reading packets one by one.
signals: HTTP or FTP traffic in the capture
first_checks: list conversations by size
export any transferred objects
scenarios: An HTTP session transfers a file of interest.
An FTP session shows commands and a data channel.
DNS queries encode data in subdomain labels.
Plaintext credentials appear in an unencrypted protocol.
A file is split across several TCP streams.

techniques.concept: Files are recognisable by their headers and footers even when the filesystem has forgotten them.
signals: a disk image or blob larger than its visible contents
first_checks: scan for known magic byte sequences
check what follows a file's declared end
scenarios: A deleted image remains in unallocated space on a disk image.
An archive is appended after the end of a picture.
Several files are concatenated into one blob.
A partially overwritten file must be reconstructed from fragments.

techniques.concept: Photographs carry structured metadata that is easy to forget and easy to read.
first_checks: dump all metadata fields
compare against what the image visually shows
scenarios: Coordinates in the metadata identify where a photo was taken.
A comment field carries text left by the author.
A thumbnail preserves content the full image no longer shows.
Editing software names and timestamps establish a timeline.

techniques.concept: Check structure before tooling; most 'stego' is data appended or stored in an extra chunk.
signals: file larger than its visible content
first_checks: compare file size against expected dimensions
list the structural chunks
scenarios: Data is stored in the least significant bits of an image.
An extra chunk holds text a viewer ignores.
Content is appended after the image's end marker.
Two nearly identical images differ only in specific pixels.
An audio file carries data in a spectrogram.

techniques.concept: A memory image captures what was true at one instant, including things never written to disk.
first_checks: identify the profile and OS version
list processes and look for anomalies
scenarios: A process dump contains credentials typed during the capture.
An injected region appears in an otherwise normal process.
Command history survives in a shell's memory.
Network connections reveal a handler that is gone from disk.

techniques.concept: Anomalies stand out against a baseline, so establish normal before hunting for strange.
signals: rare user agents or status codes
first_checks: aggregate by frequency
sort by time and look for bursts
scenarios: Web logs contain a single unusual request among many normal ones.
Authentication logs show a successful attempt after many failures.
Timestamps are inconsistent with the claimed sequence of events.
A rare user agent string appears only during the incident window.

techniques.concept: Narrow by what cannot change: architecture, signage, vegetation, sun angle.
first_checks: list every fixed feature visible
work from country to region to street
scenarios: A photo shows a recognisable skyline.
Street furniture and signage narrow the country.
Shadows and vegetation indicate hemisphere and season.
A reflection reveals detail not directly photographed.

techniques.concept: People reuse handles; correlation across platforms builds a picture no single site holds.
first_checks: search the handle across public platforms
compare writing style and timing
scenarios: The same handle appears on several public sites.
A profile picture is reused across accounts.
Public commit history links a handle to an email address.
Archived pages preserve a profile that was later edited.

techniques.concept: Infrastructure has history, and history is frequently public.
first_checks: enumerate subdomains from public sources
check certificate transparency logs
scenarios: Historical DNS records reveal a staging host.
A certificate log lists subdomains not linked anywhere.
Registration data connects two apparently separate domains.
An archived page references an endpoint that still resolves.

techniques.concept: Automate the repetitive part, but cap the depth so a zip bomb cannot exhaust the machine.
first_checks: check the compression ratio before extracting
set an extraction depth limit
scenarios: Hundreds of nested archives wrap a single file.
Each layer uses a different archive format.
Layers are password protected with the password in the previous layer.
A high compression ratio suggests a decompression bomb.

techniques.concept: Identify the language from its character set, then use an interpreter rather than reading it.
first_checks: identify the language from its distinctive characters
find a reference interpreter
scenarios: A program written in a minimal eight-instruction language.
Source consisting only of whitespace characters.
Code disguised as ordinary English prose.
A two-dimensional program whose control flow moves on a grid.

techniques.concept: An external call hands control away; state must be settled before that happens.
signals: external call before a state update
first_checks: order every state write against every external call
check for a guard modifier
scenarios: A withdrawal sends funds before zeroing the recorded balance.
A callback hook lets a recipient re-enter during transfer.
Cross-function reentrancy touches shared state via a second entry point.
A read-only view returns stale state during an in-flight call.

techniques.concept: A privileged function without an ownership check is a public function.
first_checks: list externally callable functions
check each for an ownership or role modifier
scenarios: A minting function is missing its owner-only modifier.
An initialiser can be called again by anyone after deployment.
Ownership transfer lacks a two-step confirmation.
A role check reads a variable the caller can influence.

techniques.concept: Rounding and unchecked arithmetic in accounting logic quietly redistribute value.
first_checks: trace the arithmetic on balances
test the boundaries and the rounding direction
scenarios: Share calculation rounds in the depositor's favour every time.
An unchecked block skips overflow protection on a subtraction.
Fee maths divides before multiplying, truncating value.
A first-depositor edge case sets an exploitable exchange rate.

techniques.concept: Anything exported in the manifest is reachable by any other app on the device.
first_checks: read the manifest and list exported components
check which of them touch private data
scenarios: An activity handling private data is exported without a permission.
A content provider grants read access far beyond what it needs.
A broadcast receiver acts on unauthenticated intents.
A deep link accepts parameters that bypass the login flow.

techniques.concept: On-device storage is readable given device access; encoding is not protection.
first_checks: inventory what the app writes to disk
check whether anything sensitive is stored in the clear
scenarios: Session tokens are saved in shared preferences as plain text.
A local database holds account details unencrypted.
Sensitive values are written to the system log.
A cache directory retains downloaded private documents.

techniques.concept: A secret shipped to the client is a secret the client owns.
first_checks: search extracted resources for key-shaped strings
check native libraries as well as bytecode
scenarios: An API key sits in a string resource file.
Credentials appear in decompiled application code.
A key is split across several constants and reassembled.
A native library embeds the secret to make it less obvious.

techniques.concept: Pinning is a client-side check, and client-side checks run on hardware the user controls.
first_checks: identify where pinning is implemented
check whether a debug path disables it
scenarios: The app pins a certificate in its network configuration.
Pinning is implemented in a custom trust manager.
A debug build flag disables validation entirely.
Only some endpoints are pinned, leaving others observable.
